sources: Ersner-Hershfield, Wimmer & Knutson (2009). Saving for the future self: Neural measures of future self-continuity predict temporal discounting. Social Cognitive and Affective Neuroscience 4(1). fMRI: future-self activation in a self/other region similar to another person; larger current-future difference predicted more discounting.

Hershfield et al. (2011). Increasing saving behavior through age-progressed renderings of the future self. Journal of Marketing Research 48. Four studies; in the VR study participants who met their aged avatar allocated about twice as much to a hypothetical retirement account (Hershfield, Federal Reserve panel transcript).
